comments.body:
## Fix implemented + validated (experiment + OSS prior art)

**Change:** added `authorship.build_introducing_commit_map()` — one `git log --diff-filter=A --full-history --no-merges --no-renames --format=%x1e%H --name-only -- '*.json'` pass building a {path→oldest-add-commit} map. `verify_authorship.cli` builds it once; `_resolve_commit` looks each event up and falls back to the per-event `resolve_event_commit` only when the map lacks the path (fail-closed preserved).

**Experimental validation (real store, ~7.2k events / ~30k commits):**
- Correctness: 700 sampled events, batch map == per-event resolver, **0 mismatches, 0 misses**.
- Perf: per-event resolve ≈ 910 ms/event → **~1.8h** extrapolated full run (timed out at 280s before). Batched map builds in ~1.7s; **real gate end-to-end: 2.33s** (exit 0, 4031 report entries).

**OSS prior art (single-pass git-log + parse into a map is the established remedy for per-file `git log`):**
- Hugo `bep/gitmap` (`enableGitInfo`) — one `git log --name-only` pass, ASCII record-separator framing (the `%x1e` technique used here).
- Astro Starlight `getAllNewestCommitDate` — one `git log --name-status` pass into a Map.
- Docusaurus migrating away from per-file `getFileCommitDate` (issue #11208) to an eager whole-repo read; e18e ecosystem-issues #216 names per-file `git log` as the anti-pattern.
- Internal precedent: `build_dep_graph` single-`reduce_all_tickets`-scan refactor (tests/scripts/graph/test_graph_perf.py) — mirrored by the batch-invariant test here.

Refinements adopted from the research: `-c log.showSignature=false`, `--no-merges`/`--no-renames`, `--full-history`, oldest-wins overwrite. Tests: correctness parity, add-verification, batch-invariant (0 per-event calls), empty-map fallback, never-raises. lint + typecheck green.

## Reproduction Steps
1. Mount the tickets store and run `rebar verify-identity` against the real store (~3504 events, ~29,575 tracker commits).
2. Observe the command does not complete within 280s (locally exit 124 / timeout).

**Expected:** the merge-gate completes in seconds.

**Actual:** the report loop calls `rebar.attest.authorship.resolve_event_commit` once per non-verified event, and that function runs `git log --diff-filter=A --format=%H -- <pathspec>` — a full-history traversal — per event. With N events and H commits it is O(N x H): 3504 x 29575 here. A bounded `--base HEAD~200` scan also exceeded 180s.

## Root Cause
`src/rebar/_commands/verify_authorship.py` cli() loop: for every non-`verified` event it calls `_resolve_commit` -> `authorship.resolve_event_commit` (`src/rebar/attest/authorship.py`), one `git log` subprocess over the whole tracker history each. Enforced-vs-grandfathered adds a `git merge-base --is-ancestor` subprocess per event on top.

## Fix Sketch
Resolve introducing commits in a SINGLE pass: one `git log --diff-filter=A --name-only --format=%H` over the tracker, build a {event-file-path -> commit} map, and look up per event (O(N + H)). Keep the per-event path as fail-closed fallback. Add a perf regression test at representative scale.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Introducing-commit resolution for a full-store scan is single-pass (not one git-log per event).
- [ ] `rebar verify-identity` over a store of ~3.5k events / ~30k commits completes in well under a minute.
- [ ] A test asserts the batched resolver returns the same commit SHAs as the per-event resolver on a seeded store.
- [ ] Fail-closed behaviour (unresolvable commit -> enforced) is preserved.
compiled_state.title: verify-identity gate is O(events x history): one git-log per event makes CI multi-minute
